result.title: An LLM-Based Agent for Legal Compliance Assessment: Architecture, Memory, and Evaluation in a Canadian and Quebec Context
result.summary: Checking whether a text complies with a body of law is slow when done by hand and fragile when done with keyword rules. This paper presents ComplianceAgent, the legal compliance sub-agent of COMPASS, a multi-agent framework that evaluates texts along four axes: digital sovereignty, carbon impact, compliance, and ethics. The agent relies on a large language model that scores a text on a fixed rubric, grounds its judgment in a reference legal corpus, and, when the score falls at or below a critical threshold, runs a corrective chain made of self-healing rewrites, a compliance label, an explainability report, and escalation to a human reviewer. We describe what the language model does at each step, how the memory of the agent is organized, and how the same implementation can be pointed at different reference corpora. We evaluate the agent in a Canadian and Quebec context, on a corpus of thirteen legal instruments that brings together federal and provincial texts, international treaties, and municipal documents of the City of Trois-Rivières. The evaluation relies on a hand-annotated gold standard of fifteen texts and combines classification metrics, a repeated-query stability test, retrieval precision, and a composite score. On this gold standard the agent separates every conforming text from every non-conforming one, its scores remain stable under repeated queries, and the index returns relevant passages.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ComplianceAgent：基于 LLM、固定评分量表与法条语料检索的法律合规评估子代理，低分时触发纠错重写、合规标签、可解释报告与人工升级，并在加拿大/魁北克 13 部法律文本、15 篇人工标注文本上评测分类、稳定性与检索精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 属法律合规文本的检索+评分流水线，虽涉及记忆组织与阈值触发的升级判定，但不涉及视觉细节保留、latent 推理状态生成或视觉证据筛选，亦无可核查的跨领域方法线索，故排除。
